Bivar Capital — Quantitative Research

Denmark MomentumSystematic momentum on Nasdaq Copenhagen with cash regime overlay

A long-only momentum strategy on Danish (Nasdaq Copenhagen) equities with a profitability filter, market regime overlay, and a cash allocation during bear markets. Status: Beta — launched with the EBIT>0 filter but not yet reviewed to the same depth as the site's UK/USA/Canada momentum books. 306 months of out-of-sample backtesting with monthly data. Signal at month-end, execution on the first trading day of the next month. No look-ahead bias.

Transaction costs are NOT YET modeled in this report. Unlike the site's UK, USA, and Canada momentum reports (which are net of measured stamp duty / real IBKR bid-ask spreads), every number below is gross — no commissions, no spread, no market impact, no FX conversion cost (DKK). This is a known gap, not an oversight being hidden: at an estimated ~10–12 average monthly portfolio turnover of 3–5 of 10 positions, realistic costs would meaningfully reduce the CAGR figures shown here. Do not treat the gross numbers below as investable net returns.

I. Strategy Specification

Signal: End of each month

  1. Regime check: Is the synthetic cap-weighted Danish index above its 100-day simple moving average?
    • NO → Sell all stocks. Move to cash. Hold until next month’s signal.
    • YES → Proceed to step 2.
  2. Compute momentum for every eligible stock:
    Momentum = 50% × (price / price 6 months ago − 1) + 50% × (price / price 12 months ago − 1)
  3. Filter universe:
    • Market capitalisation > 700 million DKK
    • EBIT (TTM) > 0 (operating profit positive, most recent report)
    • Nasdaq Copenhagen common stock, DKK-denominated only
  4. Select top 10 by momentum composite. Inverse-volatility weighted (126-day trailing realized daily vol, annualized).
  5. Execute on the 1st trading day of the next month: sell positions that left the portfolio, buy new ones. No transaction costs applied (see caveat above).

Live script approximation. The strategy running in denmark_momentum_signal.py uses TradingView Screener exclusively (no EODHD, no historical price database) so it can run unattended in CI without maintaining a local parquet cache. TradingView exposes no historical volatility field, so the live script cannot compute a true trailing realized-vol inverse-vol weight — it falls back to equal weight across the top 10. This report's headline methodology uses true inverse-vol weighting instead, since it is real, computable, and available from the EODHD daily price history used here. Section IX below shows the InvVol vs Equal-weight ablation directly so the gap between the live approximation and this report's headline is explicit, not hidden — the same transparency pattern used in the UK report's stamp-duty/spread section.

Why momentum works: Stocks that have risen tend to continue rising. Institutional capital flows are slow — funds take weeks to build positions. Information propagates gradually. Behavioural biases cause investors to sell winners too early and hold losers too long.
Why cash during bear markets: The MA100 regime filter identifies bear markets early — switching to cash avoids the stock drawdown entirely instead of trying to time a hedge. No official 2001+ Danish index history is cleanly available (yfinance's ^OMXC25 only starts 2016-12), so the regime index here is built locally as a cap-weighted return index from the cleaned CO universe itself — no network calls.

IX. Filter & Weighting Ablation — The EBIT / InvVol Tradeoff

Each row changes one dimension. 50/50 6M+12M momentum, top 10, >700M DKK mcap, gross of costs.

ConfigurationCAGRSharpeMaxDDAlphaNote
FULL: EBIT>0 + InvVol +17.5% 1.11 -34.6% +9.6% — headline config
EBIT>0 + Equal Weight +18.0% 1.09 -34.7% +10.1% vs InvVol: Sharpe -0.02, MaxDD -0.1pp
No EBIT + InvVol +17.3% 1.17 -31.0% +9.4% EBIT filter: CAGR +0.2pp, but MaxDD -3.5pp worse (real tradeoff, not a clean win)
NAKED: No EBIT + Equal Weight +16.9% 1.10 -31.7% +9.0% Pure momentum baseline (no filter, no InvVol)
Honest tradeoff, not a clean win. Adding the EBIT>0 filter raises CAGR and alpha but worsens max drawdown — the opposite of the UK strategy, where EBIT>0 helps on every axis. The mechanism: EBIT>0 shrinks the average eligible universe from 63 to 41 names/month, reducing diversification within the top-10 portfolio and concentrating risk. The user made an explicit, informed decision to adopt EBIT>0 for the live strategy anyway, accepting the deeper drawdown for the higher return and closer alignment with the site's other momentum books (UK, USA) which also screen on profitability.

XII. Data-Quality Audit

Two distinct EODHD bug classes found and excluded from the entire backtest universe (mcap, momentum ranking, and the regime index) — not merely flagged in a table:

  • Class 1 — implausible single-day price spikes. 14 tickers show a single-day |return| >300% or an absolute price level implausible for a DKK-denominated stock, with no corporate action (split, rights issue) on record explaining the move: AAB, AGAT, BLVIS-A, CONFRZ, CPHCAP-ST, EAC, ENALYZ, NORDIC, NRDF, OKEAC, STRAP, UNLGRP, VJBA, WIRTEK.
  • Class 2 — silently-wrong adjusted_close inflating market cap across a ticker's whole history, not just spiking on one day. 4 tickers: GYLD-A, NEWCAP, ORPHA, ROV. This class is more dangerous because it never crosses an obvious single-day-return threshold — it was caught by cross-checking implied market cap against trading volume (a company with >50B DKK mcap trading <5,000 shares/day is not plausible). NEWCAP alone carried >50% of the weight of the first-pass synthetic cap-weighted regime index in 2001 before this check was added.

Exact 999999.9999 EODHD sentinel bug (the confirmed pattern from the LSE/UK audit): none tickers found in the Danish universe.

XIII. Look-Ahead Bias Audit

Signal & Execution Timeline

Month-end (signal): Compute momentum using historical month-end prices (6 and 12 months back). Check the synthetic Danish index vs its 100-day moving average. All data is from the past. ✓

1st trading day of next month (execution): Buy/sell using next-month price data. No same-month execution. ✓

Data Sources Verified

DataSourceTimingStatus
Stock prices (momentum)EODHD adjusted closeSignal month-end and 6/12 months prior✓ Past only
Regime index (MA100)Local synthetic cap-weighted index (EODHD-derived)Signal date close vs last 100 days✓ Past only
Market capEODHD mcap_daily.parquetMonth-end snapshot✓ Past only
EBIT (TTM)EODHD quarterly, via filing_datePoint-in-time avail_date, ~60 day fallback lag✓ Past only
Trailing volatility (InvVol)EODHD daily prices, 126-day trailingSignal month-end, backward-looking only✓ Past only
Execution pricesEODHD adjusted closeNext month, after signal✓ No same-month
Conclusion: No look-ahead bias detected. Signal uses only past prices. Fundamentals use point-in-time filing dates, not period-end dates.

XIV. Risks & Caveats

  • Transaction costs NOT modeled. Every number in this report is gross. This is the single biggest known gap versus the UK/USA/Canada reports on this site — treat all figures above as an upper bound on what is investable.
  • EBIT>0 filter worsens drawdown (Section IX) — a real tradeoff the strategy has accepted for higher CAGR/alpha, not a universally positive filter like it is for UK.
  • Live script approximates InvVol with Equal Weight due to a TradingView data limitation (Section I) — the live portfolio will not track this report's headline numbers exactly.
  • Beta status. This strategy has not yet received the same depth of review as the site's other momentum books (real spread costs, liquidity sensitivity, crisis-period analysis). It is launched as Beta, not Live, specifically because of this.
  • Small, thin market. The eligible universe averages only 41 names/month with the EBIT>0 filter applied — materially smaller than the UK or US universes, which increases concentration and data-quality sensitivity per name.
  • ~25 years, multiple bear markets. Includes the dot-com bust, 2008 GFC, and 2020 COVID crash, via the synthetic regime index.
  • Concentration risk. 10 stocks, inverse-vol weighted (not equal) — low-vol names can carry a meaningfully larger share than 10%.
